This PR started on a wrong hypothesis. The corrected finding shipped instead.

fix/search-cold-start-and-aeo-geo · both halves verified against real generated output, not typecheck alone

The bug is real. The cause I assumed was wrong by 100-300x.

A HAR capture and 32 live curl probes against the deployed site showed a real, reproducible pattern: warm search requests at 0.23-0.39s, and two separate queries that spiked to 11.1-12.5 seconds with byte-identical responses to the warm case. The natural read: the route builds two full Orama indexes at module scope on every cold instance. Before writing a fix, that hypothesis got tested directly.

This PR does not claim to fix the 11-12 second stall. The real cause is most likely Vercel serverless cold-container overhead — cold init, parsing a bundle that embeds ~8.3MB of generated content — which needs a different class of fix (bundle size, Fluid Compute pre-warming) than anything an app-level index-build change can reach. What this PR does: fixes the real (small) inefficiency it found, and instruments the actual request path with a Server-Timing header + duration_ms telemetry, so the NEXT time this is observed in production, it's visible instead of invisible.

What actually shipped, and why it's still worth shipping

A real secondary bug the measurement found

fumadocs calls indexes() synchronously inside each createSearchAPI() call — so the underlying document-collection walk (source.getPages() + skills/agents/hooks/compositions) really was running twice, once per Orama variant, even though the records are identical between them. Fixed with a single memoized getIndexRecords(). This is real, verified, and worth the tens of milliseconds it saves — just not the seconds the symptom showed.

Lazy, single-flight index construction

Each Orama variant (strict/fuzzy) now builds only when a request actually needs it, memoized per warm instance. No explicit lock needed: the check-and-assign is synchronous with no await between them, so Node's single-threaded event loop cannot interleave a duplicate build.

Telemetry: the thing that actually matters going forward

signalwhere
Server-Timing: search;dur=<ms>app/api/search/route.ts response header — readable by any direct API caller
duration_ms on search:performedclient-side, debounce-settle → results-arrived (fumadocs' client wrapper cannot surface the Response object, so the server header isn't reachable from the dialog — documented, not a bug)
permanent regression test__tests__/search-cold-build.test.ts — pins the structural invariants (no eager build, one variant per request, shared doc-walk, no rebuild on repeat)

Real generated output, not just code that typechecks

Extracted from the actual built HTML of /docs/reference/skills/audit-full (complexity: "max" in the real skill data):

{
  "headline": "Audit Full",
  "dependencies": "security-patterns, architecture-patterns, quality-gates",
  "proficiencyLevel": "Expert",
  "author": { "@id": "https://github.com/yonatangross#person" },
  "publisher": { "@id": "https://orchestkit.yonyon.ai/#organization" }
}
Why this needed a real fix, not just wiring the function in. techArticleNode() references author/publisher purely by @id. Those entities were only emitted on /about, /compare and the homepage — never inside /docs/*. Real structured-data consumers (Google's Rich Results Test included) evaluate each page's JSON-LD in isolation; they do not fetch other pages to resolve an @id. Wiring the function in as originally built would have shipped dangling, unresolvable references across all ~270 docs pages. Fixed by emitting a self-contained @graph (Organization + Person + TechArticle + BreadcrumbList) on every page.
schema.org/proficiencyLevel only defines "Beginner" and "Expert" — no "Intermediate". A skill's "medium" complexity is deliberately left undefined rather than forced into either bucket.

Investigated and deliberately left unchanged

The original brief for this half was "add missing links to our providers." Two real investigations concluded that doing so, as literally stated, would have been wrong.

The content-link audit

The observation that motivated this ("0 links to posthog.com / cloudflare.com in content") measured the wrong thing. The only PostHog/Cloudflare mentions found are inside generic vendor-comparison tables in generated skill-teaching content (e.g. "Analytics | BUY: PostHog (1h) vs BUILD: custom (2-4w)") — advice to users about picking tools for their own projects, not a claim about this site's own integrations. Linking "PostHog" there would misrepresent a teaching example as an integration claim.

Also confirmed: content/docs/reference/skills/ is generator-owned (per build-docs.sh and check-docs-facts.mjs) — hand-editing it directly would repeat the exact mistake a sibling PR made with plugins/ earlier the same day.

llms.txt

Its own header comment states the design goal explicitly: kept well under the 30,000-char recommendation, pointing elsewhere for detail. Adding an integrations section would work against that stated purpose, so it was left alone.
